title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure in an automated identification system, occurring at the point where a camera-generated alert was passed to a patrol deputy for enforcement. The plate reader produced a match that was wrong by a single character, and that wrong match became the basis for a felony stop. The failure sits at the handoff between machine output and human action, not inside the model alone.

Catching it would have required the deputy to verify the alert independently before drawing a weapon, which is what the vendor itself says should happen. The facts describe a system whose alerts were treated as actionable on their own. Whether any policy required verification, and whether the deputy followed it, is not established by the reporting.

The sheriff's office attributes the misread to an illegal tinted plate cover and calls the deputy's response reasonable. Flock states that alerts should be independently verified before enforcement. That the cover caused the malfunction is the sheriff's account, not a finding, and no ruling or consequence for the deputy or the department is established.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: A 42-year-old York County, South Carolina, motorist, Steven Melvin, was detained at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the malfunction and called the deputy’s actions reasonable, while Flock said alerts should be independently verified before enforcement.
